questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Das ist ___ Bruder. (ich)
questions.explanation: Masculine nominative Bruder takes mein from the first-person possessive stem.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Das ist ___ Schwester. (ich)
questions.explanation: Feminine nominative Schwester takes meine.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Das ist ___ Kind. (ich)
questions.explanation: Neuter nominative Kind takes mein.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Das sind ___ Eltern. (ich)
questions.explanation: Plural Eltern takes meine.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Ist das ___ Tasche? (du)
questions.explanation: Feminine nominative Tasche takes deine from the du possessive stem.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Ich sehe ___ Vater. (du)
questions.explanation: Masculine accusative Vater takes deinen.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Wir besuchen ___ Freunde. (er)
questions.explanation: Plural Freunde takes seine from the er possessive stem.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Sie sucht ___ Schlüssel. (sie)
questions.explanation: Masculine accusative Schlüssel takes ihren from the feminine singular possessive stem ihr-.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Wir sprechen mit ___ Lehrerin. (wir)
questions.explanation: mit governs the dative, and feminine dative uses unserer.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct possessive form: Kommt ihr mit ___ Auto? (ihr)
questions.explanation: mit governs the dative, and neuter dative Auto uses eurem.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses aufstehen?
questions.explanation: In a main clause, aufstehen separates: the finite form stehe is second and auf goes to the end.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses einkaufen?
questions.explanation: The separable prefix ein moves to the end in the main clause: Sie kauft … ein.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses fernsehen?
questions.explanation: The verb fernsehen separates in a main clause: Wir sehen … fern.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses anrufen in the imperative?
questions.explanation: The informal imperative of anrufen is Ruf … an, with the prefix at the end.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses anfangen?
questions.explanation: The prefix of anfangen separates in a main clause.

questions.prompt: Which infinitive is separable?
questions.explanation: aufstehen contains the separable prefix auf; many inseparable prefixes include be- and ver-.

questions.prompt: Which prefix is commonly inseparable?
questions.explanation: ver- is a commonly inseparable prefix, while auf-, ein- and an- are common separable prefixes.

questions.prompt: How does aufstehen appear after a modal?
choices: Ich muss auf um sechs stehen.
questions.explanation: After a modal, the complete infinitive aufstehen remains together at the end.

questions.prompt: Which preposition means “with” and takes the dative?
questions.explanation: mit means “with” and governs the dative: mit dem Bus.

questions.prompt: Which preposition means “for” and takes the accusative?
questions.explanation: für governs the accusative: ein Geschenk für meinen Bruder.

questions.prompt: Which preposition means “without” and takes the accusative?
questions.explanation: ohne governs the accusative: Kaffee ohne Zucker.

questions.prompt: Which preposition means “from / out of” and takes the dative?
questions.explanation: aus governs the dative and often marks origin or movement out of an enclosed place.

questions.prompt: Which preposition means “at / near” and takes the dative?
questions.explanation: bei governs the dative: Sie arbeitet bei einer Firma.

questions.prompt: Which preposition normally introduces a destination city?
questions.explanation: nach is commonly used with cities and most countries without an article: nach Berlin.

questions.prompt: Which preposition normally introduces origin from a city?
questions.explanation: aus is used for origin from a city or country: Ich komme aus Berlin.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “at the doctor’s”?
questions.explanation: beim is the contraction of bei dem, and bei dem Arzt means at the doctor’s / with the doctor.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “to the station”?
questions.explanation: zum is the contraction of zu dem; zum Bahnhof means to the station.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means “in the city”?
questions.explanation: A stationary location uses the dative: in der Stadt.

questions.prompt: What is the informal singular imperative of kommen?
questions.explanation: The informal singular imperative of kommen is Komm!

questions.prompt: What is the informal singular imperative of machen?
questions.explanation: The informal singular imperative of machen is Mach!

questions.prompt: What is the informal singular imperative of lesen?
questions.explanation: lesen has the stem-vowel change e to ie in the informal singular imperative: Lies!

questions.prompt: What is the formal imperative of sprechen?
questions.explanation: The formal imperative uses the infinitive plus Sie: Sprechen Sie!

questions.prompt: What is the plural informal imperative of warten?
questions.explanation: The ihr imperative uses the second-person plural present form without the pronoun: Wartet!

questions.prompt: What does “Seien Sie bitte ruhig!” mean?
questions.explanation: Seien Sie is the formal imperative of sein, and ruhig means quiet.

questions.prompt: What is the comparative of klein?
questions.explanation: The regular comparative adds -er: klein becomes kleiner.

questions.prompt: What is the comparative of groß?
questions.explanation: The comparative of groß is größer, with an umlaut and -er.

questions.prompt: What is the superlative form used after a definite article for schnell?
questions.explanation: Attributive superlatives use -st- plus the appropriate adjective ending: der schnellste.

questions.prompt: What does “Das Wetter ist kalt.” mean?
questions.explanation: kalt is the predicate adjective meaning cold.

questions.prompt: What does “ein gutes Buch” mean?
questions.explanation: Buch is neuter and the indefinite article plus attributive adjective gives ein gutes Buch in the nominative/accusative.

questions.prompt: What does “eine kleine Wohnung” mean?
questions.explanation: Wohnung is feminine and the attributive adjective after eine takes -e: eine kleine Wohnung.

questions.prompt: Which adjective means “new”?
questions.explanation: neu means new; alt means old.

questions.prompt: Which adjective means “slow”?
questions.explanation: langsam means slow.
